resources.string: Your network. One tap closer to awake.
No devices yet.\nScan the subnet or add a device by its MAC address.
Double-tap to wake · Hold for shortcuts and editing

Discovery is best effort, not a complete network inventory. Sleeping devices and devices blocking probes may not respond. PTR DNS and unicast mDNS are tried; some devices have no published name.

Android 10 and newer prevent ordinary apps from reading the ARP table. Those phones cannot automatically retrieve arbitrary device MAC addresses. Enter the MAC from your router or the target device using Add device or Edit device. Older Android versions may expose cached ARP entries. A phone model name is used for this phone if it has no DNS name.

Previously discovered devices remain in the list. “Saved MAC” is not a freshly verified address: DHCP and different networks with the same subnet can make cached details stale. Verify the MAC before waking or creating a shortcut.

An active VPN is preferred over Wi-Fi. Select its routed LAN subnet, not just the tunnel address. For a full-tunnel VPN, enter the remote LAN subnet manually. Layer-3 VPNs do not expose remote MAC addresses, and many block broadcasts. Wake over VPN requires the VPN/router to forward directed broadcasts to the LAN, or a suitable layer-2 VPN. This app cannot bypass that restriction.

WOL must be enabled in the target firmware and network adapter. A sent packet is not proof the device woke. Wi-Fi clients, sleeping phones and isolated guest networks often do not support WOL.

Only scan networks you own or have permission to scan. IPv4 only; ranges larger than 4,096 hosts must be narrowed explicitly. Shortcuts send without opening this screen; failures produce a brief Android message.
